enchodus-machairus:study:1.title: A new species of Enchodus from the Western Interior Seaway of North America and a taxonomic revision of Enchodus dirus , Leidy, 1857 (Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology, 2026)

facts.statement: Enchodus machairus is a newly described species of the fish genus Enchodus.
The species Enchodus machairus was named by Nelson, Murray and Sims.
Enchodus machairus lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
The type locality of Enchodus machairus is the Niobrara Formation in Kansas, United States.
facts.quote:
Type locality: Niobrara Formation
Country: United States
Region: Kansas

facts.statement: Species of Enchodus were abundant in Late Cretaceous marine ecosystems worldwide.
facts.quote: Species of Enchodus flourished during the Late Cretaceous, where they were a widespread component of marine ecosystems worldwide

facts.statement: There is limited evidence that some Enchodus may have survived into the Paleocene or Eocene, though this could represent reworked Cretaceous material.
facts.quote: there is some evidence that they may have survived to the Paleocene or Eocene; however, this may just represent reworked Cretaceous material.

facts.statement: The prominent fangs, streamlined body and large eyes indicate that Enchodus was a predatory fish.
facts.quote: These fangs, along with a long sleek body and large eyes, suggest Enchodus was a predatory species.

facts.statement: Fossilized stomach contents of larger predators frequently contain Enchodus remains, showing it was preyed upon by sharks, other fish, mosasaurs, plesiosaurs and seabirds.
facts.quote: remains of Enchodus are commonly found among the stomach contents of larger predators, including sharks, other bony fish, mosasaurs, plesiosaurs and seabirds such as Baptornis advenus

facts.statement: Enchodus fossils have been recovered from Late Cretaceous rocks in many U.S. states, including Kansas where Enchodus machairus was found.
facts.quote: Enchodus remains have been recovered from most US states with fossiliferous Late Cretaceous rocks, including Kansas

facts.statement: Species of Enchodus are generally divided into two clades, a North American clade and a Mediterranean clade.
facts.quote: Species of Enchodus are generally classified into two different clades, the North American and the Mediterranean.

facts.statement: The separation of North American and Mediterranean Enchodus clades may reflect several isolated evolutionary events during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: It has been proposed that this distinction is the result of several isolated events between the two populations over the Late Cretaceous.

facts.statement: Enchodus is an extinct genus of fish belonging to the family Enchodontidae.
facts.quote: Enchodus es un género extinto de peces de la familia Enchodontidae.

facts.statement: Enchodus machairus lived during the Coniacian to early Campanian stages of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: E. machairus Nelson, Murray & Sims, 2026 - Coniacian to Early Campanian of Kansas, US (Niobrara Formation)

facts.statement: Enchodus machairus was formally described in 2026 by Luke E. Nelson, Alison M. Murray, and Megan E. Sims.
Fossils of Enchodus machairus have been recovered from the Niobrara Formation in Kansas, United States.
facts.quote: E. machairus Nelson, Murray & Sims, 2026 - Coniacian to Early Campanian of Kansas, US (Niobrara Formation)

facts.statement: Members of the genus Enchodus are characterized by large fangs on the front of the upper and lower jaws and on the palate, giving them a saber‑toothed appearance.
facts.quote: Los atributos más notables del género son los grandes colmillos en la parte frontal de las mandíbulas superior e inferior y en los huesos palatinos

facts.statement: Some Enchodus species, such as E. zinensis, reached lengths of about 172.2 cm (67.8 in).
facts.quote: E. zinensis alcanzaba los 172,2 cm (67,8 pulgadas) de longitud

facts.statement: It is debated whether post‑Cretaceous Enchodus fossils represent true survival or are merely reworked material.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, también se ha sugerido que todos los registros posteriores al Cretácico son solo material reelaborado
